title: Graceful evacuation and delay-tolerant routing for dedicated control planes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a coordinated "graceful evacuation" flow for Dedicated and Private control planes to minimize customer-visible impact during region-level maintenance, network partitions, or hardware blackouts. The flow must integrate SLO-aware decisions, tenant QoS classes, KV-cache checkpointing, and delay-tolerant routing to warm standby regions while avoiding cascading overloads.
acceptance_criteria: A documented evacuation protocol that can be executed automated or manually via the Console
Control-plane can drain 80% of active sessions within target window while maintaining P99 latency SLO for high-priority tenants
KV cache snapshot/restore completes for active tenants within tolerated window and does not cause sustained CPU/GPU load spikes
Circuit breakers trigger per-tenant early shedding to protect sibling tenants; metrics emitted to Prometheus and visible in Console
Automated failover (cold-to-warm) for up to 2 regions verified in runbook and verified with chaos test in staging
design_notes: We prioritize minimizing tail-latency for high-tier tenants while allowing best-effort degradation for low-tier tenants during evacuation.
Evacuation decision will be SLO-driven: burn-rate + sustained error rate + infra health signals feed a policy engine (initial PoC uses a rule-based engine; consider replacing with ML if needed).
KV cache transfer: prefer streaming incremental snapshots to object storage (S3) with manifest + resumable chunking rather than large monolithic dumps to avoid spikes.
Routing: implement 'delay-tolerant routing' where best-effort traffic is redirected to warm standbys and client SDKs receive a 'degraded-affinity' hint to use relaxed timeout/retry behavior.
Circuit breaker model: per-tenant, per-region breaker with incremental shedding thresholds (5%, 25%, 60%) and cooldown windows; breakers emit structured events to the Control Plane Event Bus.
We will not rely on global consensus for evacuation state; use a leaderless, monotonic token in etcd to avoid long tail coordination.
Security: all snapshot transfers must use customer KMS-wrapped keys; ensure audit events for snapshot initiation and restore are recorded in audit logs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (PoC) - 2 weeks: implement rule-based SLO policy, simple KV streaming to S3, and per-tenant breaker with local shedding. Test in staging with one dedicated tenant pool.
Phase 2 - 4 weeks: integrate routing hints into SDK and Console UI for runbook ops; implement warm-standby registration and basic traffic redirect tests across two regions.
Phase 3 - 3 weeks: add canary draining (5% traffic shadowing), GA-grade observability (dashboards, traces, SLO dashboards), and runbook automation triggers.
Phase 4 - 2 weeks: harden snapshot/restore performance, chaos testing across multi-region partition scenarios, finalize runbook and oncall playbook.
Rollout: progressive rollout to non-critical customers first, then to P1/P0 tenants after verification.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Streaming KV snapshots to S3 increases the window during which data is not local; tradeoff vs faster bulk copy which causes CPU/GPU spikes.
Leaderless coordination reduces worst-case latencies but may lead to temporary split-brain interpretations of evacuation status; we'll mitigate by monotonic tokens and conflict resolution rules.
Per-tenant shedding requires accurate tenant classification; misclassification could unfairly impact customers. We'll add telemetry to monitor correctness.
SDK changes for delay-tolerant routing could increase client complexity; provide clear SDK defaults and fallbacks to avoid developer friction.
